ME-2024-LD462.policyArea: ADMINISTRATION, CREDITABLE SERVICE, STATE RETIREMENT SYSTEM
ME-2024-LD462.aiSummary: The bill would change Maine retirement rules so some state retirement members could get service credit for time served in the U.S. Armed Forces during operations in Lebanon and Grenada. It affects members of the Maine Public Employees Retirement System who served during those conflict periods. The Lebanon dates are August 21, 1982 to February 26, 1984, and the Grenada dates are October 25, 1983 to December 15, 1983.

ME-2024-LD260.aiSummary: This resolution would ask voters to amend the Maine Constitution to bar the state and local governments from denying equal rights based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, disability, ancestry, or national origin. It would affect Maine residents and state and local governments. If approved by voters, the change would become part of the state constitution.

ME-2024-LD2237.policyArea: EVIDENCE, OPERATING UNDER INFLUENCE, ORAL FLUID TESTING
ME-2024-LD2237.aiSummary: The bill would let police use oral fluid tests, along with blood, breath, and urine tests, to check for alcohol or drug use in some OUI cases. It applies to aircraft operators and people who hunt, and the text also covers watercraft, snowmobile, and ATV cases. It would also let these test results be used as evidence in court under the same general testing rules.

ME-2024-LD1980.policyArea: LAW ENFORCEMENT, PERSONNEL, RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, WELLNESS
ME-2024-LD1980.aiSummary: The bill would create a Law Enforcement Retention Advisory Council to advise the Public Safety commissioner on ways to improve police recruitment, retention, and wellness. It would also require death certificates to show whether a person had worked as a police officer, firefighter, or emergency medical worker. In addition, it would add wellness training and critical incident debriefing to basic law enforcement training and fund one wellness coordinator position at the Maine Criminal Justice Academy.

ME-2024-LD1764.policyArea: CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION, PROGRAMS, STAFFING
ME-2024-LD1764.aiSummary: The bill would set minimum staff-to-student ratios for career and technical education centers and regions in Maine, with one ratio for sites with fewer than 1,000 students and another for larger sites. It would also let a center or region use a different ratio if it fits the program’s industry standard and the Education Commissioner approves it. Starting in 2025, centers and regions would have to report funding gaps each year, and the Department of Education would use available funds to help meet the staffing rules, with preference for smaller programs.

ME-2024-LD1720.policyArea: HEALTH CARE SERVICES, LONG-TERM CARE, WORKFORCE TRAINING
ME-2024-LD1720.aiSummary: The bill would give long-term care workers, including nurses, certified nursing assistants, direct care workers, and housekeeping and dietary staff, access to the state retirement system and state health plan. It would also require MaineCare to pay nursing homes and residential care facilities for staff training and interpreter services, including training for nurse aide work, direct care work, and English as a second language. The Department of Professional and Financial Regulation would have to offer the written nursing assistant exam in French, Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, and Filipino by January 1, 2026.

ME-2024-LD1056.policyArea: ITEMS TAXED, PREPAID WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATION, SALES AND USE TAX
ME-2024-LD1056.aiSummary: The bill would say that prepaid wireless phone service is subject to Maine sales tax, and it would add a plain definition for that kind of service. It would also say that this service is not subject to the state service provider tax. The change would apply back to sales on or after July 1, 2022, but taxes already paid before the effective date would not be refunded or credited.
